analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5938, up 0.0175 from the supplied 0.5763 reference. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.640, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.635, Electronics 0.420, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.680. Electronics remains the weakest category. Validation-selected fusion is promising, but the supplied results do not reveal selected weights or isolate fusion's contribution from checkpoint variation. The grid guarantees local HR@10 nondecrease versus equal weighting on identical checkpoints and cases; it does not guarantee future host or held-out improvement. Reported training allocation consumed 2048.88 GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Retains independently trained LightGCN and SASRec experts. LightGCN uses a learned mixture of depths 0–2, item biases, recency-weighted histories, target-excluded training profiles, and 32-negative sampled softmax. SASRec uses two causal attention blocks, 50-dimensional embeddings, length-50 histories, and 16-negative sampled softmax. After strictly reloading each expert's selected checkpoint, caches validation candidate ranks and selects a category-specific reciprocal-rank fusion weight from {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, with constant 60. Selection maximizes HR@10, breaking ties by proximity to 0.5 and then smaller graph weight. Metadata persists weights and grid results; the generated predictor uses the shared loader for all four dataset routes. Deterministic fixtures cover fusion, ranking, padding, metadata loading, and predictor parity.
